frameworks.name: Hybrid Model (1.0 / 2.0 Transition)
frameworks.definition: A two-phase transition from in-person to online business: 1.0 keeps in-person sales while shifting delivery to remote; 2.0 makes both acquisition and delivery fully remote.

claims.text: Alex Hormozi argues that an in-person service business can transition to remote delivery without changing its sales channel first: sell exactly as you currently do in person, but deliver the service remotely. This is the lowest-risk starting point because it preserves the trust and conversion dynamics of in-person selling while eliminating the geographic constraint on delivery.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Service business currently acquiring clients in person
Founder is new to online/remote delivery
Delivery can be meaningfully conducted remotely (e.g., coaching, classes)
claims.mechanism: In-person sales retains inherent local trust (prospect assumes you are a real person who is not going anywhere), so conversion rates and lead costs remain favorable during the transition; only the delivery channel changes.
bounded_by: Does not apply if the service is inherently location-dependent and cannot be delivered remotely (e.g., hands-on physical therapy, in-studio tattoo)

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that in-person sales channels produce materially better conversion rates and lower lead costs than remote/online sales channels because of inherent local trust: prospects assume a local business is a real entity that will not disappear.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Prospect is a local resident encountering a local in-person business
claims.mechanism: Geographic co-location signals permanence and accountability; the prospect cannot easily dismiss the provider as a scam because the provider physically exists in their community.
bounded_by: Does not hold when the online brand has built equivalent trust signals (e.g., large social proof, strong testimonials, established reputation)

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that for a service business owner with no existing online audience and no content posted, advertising and letting people know about the offering is the primary constraint on revenue and must be the first focus, regardless of whether the service or course content is fully built.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Operator is brand new to online business or content creation
No existing digital audience or content library
claims.mechanism: Without lead flow, no product quality or course completeness matters; nobody buys what nobody knows exists.
bounded_by: Does not apply when a business already has inbound lead volume that exceeds close capacity

claims.text: Alex Hormozi used a hybrid model during COVID-19 lockdowns at Gym Launch: gyms sold individual appointments in person (leveraging in-person trust and existing client relationships) and delivered group classes remotely, enabling revenue continuity when in-person group delivery was legally prohibited.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: In-person group delivery was prohibited (COVID lockdown context)
bounded_by: Context was forced by regulatory constraint, not elected as an optimization strategy

examples.text: During COVID-19, Alex Hormozi applied the hybrid model at Gym Launch: gyms could not hold in-person group classes, but could conduct individual one-on-one appointments. Gym Launch gyms sold clients in person during those individual appointments and then delivered coaching and classes remotely. This allowed them to maintain revenue and client relationships despite the restriction on in-person group delivery.

practices.text: If you are transitioning an in-person service business to online, start by keeping your existing in-person sales process intact and simply switch your delivery to remote. Do not rebuild your acquisition channel until the remote delivery model is working.
For a brand-new online business with no audience, prioritize advertising and awareness above building or perfecting the product or course content.
Phase the transition to fully remote in two steps: 1.0 is in-person sales with remote delivery; 2.0 is remote sales with remote delivery. Do not attempt both transitions simultaneously.
